clue.text: Person set against work -difficult problem!

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a musical work
a poser is a puzzling question that is hard to answer

explanation.surface: Someone resists a job, exclaiming that it is a real headache.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets themselves against a plan is its opponent or objector.

clue.text: Gemstone displayed without a twitch of an eye

indicators.note: the gem is shown outside the twitch, so the gem word wraps around it

parts.note: opal is a milky iridescent gemstone
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A jewel shown off without anyone so much as blinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sight or the eye, as in the nerve that connects eye to brain.

clue.text: A gratuity for just being there

explanation.surface: A tip handed over merely for turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift or tip given freely is one sense; being in attendance, rather than absent, is the other.

clue.text: Country is nonchalant, up to a point

parts.note: S for south is a point of the compass

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: airy means casual and unconcerned

explanation.surface: A nation that is relaxed only up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up to a point' looks like a phrase meaning partly; 'up' reverses AIRY to YRIA and 'to a point' attaches S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation whose capital is Damascus.

clue.text: Marine possibly turning colour due to excess

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of marine may be arranged another way
turning means the colour word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A marine perhaps changing colour from overindulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MARINE into REMAIN and 'turning' reverses RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left over beyond what is needed is surplus, the leftover part.

clue.text: Small matters slide at break

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it up, so the letters of slide and at are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Minor points about a slide going on at playtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a school playtime but signals that SLIDE and AT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor particulars or points are the fine items that make up a whole.

clue.text: One making much of a period with royalty

parts.note: a dot is a full stop, called a period in American English
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone making the most of a spell spent among royals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fondly lavishes affection on another person is a fond admirer.

clue.text: Board accepting a fall may be enlightened

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the board word holds the fall word

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a board at dinner
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: A committee admits a stumble and might learn from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone capable of being taught can be educated or instructed.

clue.text: Young child standing over a princess

indicators.note: in a down clue standing over places the child word above the a

parts.note: an infant is a very young child

explanation.surface: A small child standing over a royal daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish or Portuguese title for a king's daughter who is not heir.

clue.text: Follow progress

explanation.surface: A two-word motto: come after, and get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after in line, as an heir does, is one sense; to do well and prosper is the other.

clue.text: A statement, article, or letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
taken as written
EM is the spelt-out name of the letter M, also a printer's measure

explanation.surface: A list of grammatical choices: a statement, an article, or a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proposition stated and then proved in mathematics or logic.

clue.text: Deal in used cars

explanation.surface: A second-hand car dealer's line of business.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal in goods is to trade them, often illicitly; vehicles moving on the roads make up the flow of road users.

clue.text: Gallant old showman

explanation.surface: A dashing veteran entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Chevalier was a French singer and actor of music hall and film fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant knight or courtly man was called by the French word for horseman; the old entertainer is Maurice Chevalier.

clue.text: Nobody will receive can opener as present

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the word for nobody holds the letter inside it

parts.note: nobody means none, not one person

indicators.note: an opener is what starts something, so the first letter of can is taken

explanation.surface: Nobody will accept a tin opener as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift but is the present time, as in the phrase 'for the nonce', meaning for now.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'for the nonce' means for the time being, so the word names the current occasion.

clue.text: Security device left at church

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lock left on at the church door.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple bar fastening for a door or gate keeps it shut securely.

clue.text: New fitting ready, hang a decorative plant

indicators.note: a new fitting suggests something rearranged, so the letters of ready and hang are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A gardener says the new bracket is set up, so hang the ornamental shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering shrub with big round heads of blue, pink or white blossoms.

clue.text: Speed with which the managers aim to score here

parts.note: to dart is to move swiftly
a board of directors manages a company

explanation.surface: The pace at which company bosses try to hit their targets.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts players throw at a circular target, trying to rack up points on it.

clue.text: Memorable revolutionary character

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: An unforgettable figure who was a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Feast days were printed in red in old calendars, hence a red-letter day is a special one.
explanation.definitionFit: A special day worth remembering is called this, from the festivals marked in red.

clue.text: Suggest the German newspaper leader was devious

parts.note: to mean something is to signify or imply it
der is a German word for the
ED, short for editor, the person who heads a newspaper

explanation.surface: Implying that a German paper's chief was underhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devious' here keeps its old sense of winding and straying from the direct path.
explanation.definitionFit: Devious literally means straying from the straight road, as a winding river or wandering walker does.

clue.text: Fabulous creature, but without standing

parts.note: a creature of fable with a fish's tail instead of legs cannot stand up

explanation.surface: A creature of legend that has no social status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without standing' seems to mean without status, but the legend's sea-maiden has a tail, not legs to stand on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea-dwelling being of folklore, half woman and half fish.

clue.text: Loving a large number, love turned sour

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: turned means the letters of sour are changed round

explanation.surface: Affection for a crowd, but romance has gone sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing romantic or passionate desire, full of affection.

clue.text: Three? Bad number!

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of three are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone superstitious complaining that three is an unlucky figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas was an early anaesthetic, used to deaden feeling in surgical patients.

clue.text: Listing what may be done at last

definitions.text: what may be done at last

explanation.surface: A tilted list of jobs to finish off eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a cobbler's foot-shaped block, on which shoes get new heels; a ship listing leans over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship tilting to one side leans this way; a shoemaker fitting new heels at his foot-shaped block does this.

clue.text: Set right with regard to the outfit

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to
a dress is an outfit

explanation.surface: Correcting someone about their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy a wrong or imbalance is to correct it.

clue.text: A woman carrier in Burlington House

indicators.note: in places the builder's word inside the abbreviation for the Academy

parts.note: Burlington House in London is home to the Royal Academy of Arts, abbreviated RA
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A female porter working at a London gallery building.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House, on Piccadilly in London, houses the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female first name, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Front men making a charge

explanation.surface: Soldiers at the head of an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading group of an advance is its point; to lead an attack is likewise to head it.

clue.text: Music maker creating a stir

indicators.note: creating suggests making something new from the letters of a stir

explanation.surface: A musician causing a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A sitar is a long-necked Indian lute.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked stringed instrument from India.

clue.text: One knows them to be well-informed

definitions.text: One knows them to be well-informed

parts.words: One knows them to be well-informed
parts.note: the idiom of knowing these, from sailing rigging, means being experienced and in the know

explanation.surface: A remark about people one recognises as knowledgeable.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'know the ropes' is to understand how things work.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of rigging on a sailing ship, which every competent sailor had to learn.

clue.text: In general anxiety about the medico

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for anxiety goes around the doctor

parts.note: angst is a general feeling of dread or anxiety
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: Widespread worry concerning the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as a phrase, but 'In' alone defines and 'general' belongs with 'anxiety'.
explanation.definitionFit: Among and in the midst of are interchangeable prepositions, as 'in the crowd' or 'among the crowd'.

clue.text: Unequalled team's beef

parts.note: top means best, without equal
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: The champion team's complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like a grievance but is the meat; topside is a lean cut from the hindquarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean cut taken from the upper thigh of the cow, often roasted.

clue.text: Hopelessness assailing the pilgrim

explanation.surface: Gloom attacking a traveller on a religious journey.
explanation.walkthrough: In Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, Giant Despair captures and torments the pilgrim Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter loss of hope is despondency; Bunyan's giant of that name imprisons and beats the pilgrim.

clue.text: Note evidence of leaves

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
signs are indications or evidence of something

explanation.surface: A musical note marking the arrival of autumn foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb: quits a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit one's post formally is to step down or depart.
